Item 58 names one evidence file for the engine pair: out/pip_pins_openmm_cuda_requires.txt. That file exists, so item 58's second branch applies: the plain engine pin must be the exact version the file says openmm-cuda==8.1.1.12 requires. The file does not say. Its 35 lines are a per-version listing of the docking code (lightdock), with its pinned release, its five build requirements and its two published files. It names no engine version, no requirement of openmm-cuda, and no wheel for the box. Item 58 then binds: the build changes nothing in the pinned list, says so, and the gate rules again. I therefore left the list, its comment and its checker exactly as build 10 has them, including openmm==8.2.0 with openmm-cuda==8.1.1.12, the pair launch 1 could not resolve. The selftest case of item 58 is also not written: it must assert that the engine pin equals the version quoted in the comment as the one openmm-cuda requires, and no evidence states such a version. The gate must rule on the pair, with evidence that actually reports what openmm-cuda==8.1.1.12 requires, before launch 2 is considered. Launch 2 is not authorised by this build: the install would fail again at the same step.
POSSIBLE OPERATOR SLIP, REPORTED, NOT PATCHED. The content of the file named for the engine evidence is a listing of the docking code. Out of pip_pins_resolve_build10.txt, the operator's joint resolve of build 10's pins, also fails on the docking code, not on the engine: it reports no usable version of lightdock==0.9.4 in the environment it ran. I did not act on either file beyond the rule above, and I added no pin, name or version of my own.
WHAT I DID CHANGE, AND NOTHING ELSE (item 61). This is an in-place edit of build 10, in four places.
(1) The declared system packages (item 59), now five: the shell's list at onbox_m4.sh line 348, with a five-line comment above it, and the matching list this program records at run_m4.py line 486, with a three-line comment. The two added names are the C compiler and the python headers, because the docking code ships no ready-built package for this python and is compiled on the box from its source archive.
(2) Where version labels come from (item 60). A new flag on the run state, set only after the install and the start-up check both pass (run_m4.py lines 1360 to 1364 and line 2832). The version reader is rewritten to take versions from two sources only, both of this run: the report the installer writes, and the metadata of the installed packages once that install has finished (lines 1652 to 1705). The reason text for a version that cannot be had is new (lines 1514 to 1527), and the label builder now gives that reason when this run installed nothing (lines 1569 to 1619). Launch 1 wrote the box image's own prediction library version, 0.6.0, into a run that installed nothing; that cannot happen now.
(3) The redocking check's record on a run that ends early (item 54). A new writer and its reason text (run_m4.py lines 4276 to 4330), called by the closing stage when that file is absent (lines 4333 to 4342) and by the close-from-disk route after the launcher's own timer (lines 4626 to 4632). Every run that ends with code 2 or code 3 now leaves that file, with no measured value, the published placement, the tolerance and the reason it was never compared.
(4) The planted cases those three changes need: the system-package list parsed from the shell's own text, with a sixth name and a missing name both refused (lines 7300 to 7324); the version sources, one planted report giving jax 0.4.35 and one failed install giving null with its reason for each of the four keys (lines 6154 to 6206); the redocking record asserted in the three install-failure flows and in the timer flow (lines 5824 to 5863); and one line marking the planted record state as past its install (line 6046).
No other line of either file moved. Nothing was renamed or reordered.
SELFTEST COUNT. Build 10 had 677 of 677. Build 11 has 740 of 740, all passing, in 14.8 seconds, well under the 300 second limit: 63 more checks, 36 from the redocking record in the three install-failure flows, 2 from the timer flow, 14 from the version sources, 5 from the system-package list, and 6 from the record keys those flows read.
PROJECTED WALL-CLOCK, unchanged, from the ceiling each stage is held to. Installing, downloading and the start-up check: at most 1,800 s. Controls (60 s sleep, empty run, unit statement): about 70 s. Redocking check, serial then parallel: at most 700 s. Per-pair docking and analysis: at most 600 s, at most 250 s per pair. Prediction timings: at most 2,000 s. Dynamics timings: at most 1,600 s, at most 600 s per complex. Storage and closing: at most 200 s. Margin: 400 s. Total at most 7,200 s, realistically 4,000 to 6,300 s, about USD 2.20 to 3.50 at 1.99 per hour.
RECORDS, all under results_m4/out/: 9 records through the shared writer in a run that finishes (the redocking check, the four inputs, and one each for the sleep check, the empty run and the unit statement). A run that ends early leaves the same nine, the redocking record void. Plus the validity file, the summary, the done marker and the environment note; the pair evidence with 3 sequence files and 3 structure files; the install log, the installer's download report, the system-package hashes, the parameter-marker record; 5 raw rank tables and 5 pose files; 3 engine rate files; one log per tool call.
ROWS, one line each, 22 in a run that finishes: 2 control rows, 2 redocking rows, 3 docking rows, 9 prediction rows (3 pairs x 3 seeds), 3 dynamics rows, 3 storage rows.
A rerun on the same box is never a replication, and nothing in these files calls it one."}
